clue.text: The Ante-Room doctor, first to take fruit

parts.note: Dr William Curran is the physician in Kate O'Brien's novel The Ante-Room

indicators.note: first to means only the opening letter of the word take is wanted

explanation.surface: A doctor in an Irish novel is the first to help himself to some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to' picks the T of 'take'. The Ante-Room (1934) is Kate O'Brien's novel set in Limerick, whose Dr Curran falls for a married woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A small dried seedless grape used in baking is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Gentleman Jim the boxer from Oregon, back in court

indicators.note: in tells us the court's abbreviation surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: OR is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Oregon
to back a horse is to bet on it

explanation.surface: A famous boxer from the American West is returning to a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a direction, returning, but it is the verb meaning to wager on something; 'in' is the container signal and 'from' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: James J. Corbett, nicknamed Gentleman Jim, was world heavyweight champion in the 1890s.

clue.text: Making a comeback, this writer with new Rebus novel

parts.note: a resurrection is a return to life, a comeback
this writer is the setter referring to themself, so ME

explanation.surface: An author returns to the bookshelves with a fresh crime story featuring Inspector Rebus.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector John Rebus is Ian Rankin's Edinburgh detective; Resurrection Men (2002) is one of the series.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of one of Ian Rankin's detective books starring Rebus.

clue.text: Loose tag one wears to support subversive literature

indicators.note: the shuffled letters wear the next piece, so it sits inside them
loose means the letters of tag are set free to rearrange

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a prop is something that supports

explanation.surface: A loose label worn on a garment is propping up some seditious pamphlets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose' rearranges the three letters to AGT, which 'wears' the one inside to make AGIT; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Political propaganda, especially communist pamphlets and posters, aims to stir up subversion.

clue.text: What Morrison's name was changed into

indicators.note: changed signals that the four letters of into are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about what a famous novelist's name was altered to.
explanation.walkthrough: The novelist born Chloe Wofford took the baptismal name Anthony, shortened it, and published under her married surname Morrison.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nobel-winning American author of Beloved published under this first name.

clue.text: Snack Vergible Woods put together

explanation.surface: A light snack assembled by someone named Vergible Woods.
explanation.walkthrough: In Zora Neale Hurston's Their Eyes Were Watching God, Vergible Woods is known as Tea Cake; 'put together' joins the two words of the nickname into one.
explanation.definitionFit: A toasted sweet bun is a light snack, and Janie's third husband in Hurston's novel goes by that nickname, written as two words and here closed up.

clue.text: Argo as myth disturbed a poet

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters of Argo as myth are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: The story of the ship Argo, treated as legend, unsettles a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard was an eighteenth-century English poet.

clue.text: Grace raised excellent spirogyra for one

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written AI with the 1 read as I
spirogyra is an example of a green alga

explanation.surface: A gardener lifts some first-rate pond weed out of the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns the whole run AIALGA upwards. A1 for first-rate is written AI in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Aglaia is one of the three Graces of Greek myth, goddess of splendour.

clue.text: Case for Holmes one re-examined cryptically?

definitions.text: Case for Holmes one re-examined cryptically?

parts.words: Case for Holmes one re-examined cryptically?
parts.note: a Sherlock Holmes case title read cryptically: one (A) study, a re-examination, placed in the colour red

explanation.surface: A Sherlock Holmes case taken up again and puzzled over.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful reading: a study is an examination, and scarlet is red, which the clue hints at with 're-'.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1887 novel is the first of Conan Doyle's stories featuring Holmes and Watson.

clue.text: Complex subject chosen by Turner?

parts.note: elect means chosen, as in the president-elect
J. M. W. Turner was a Royal Academician, abbreviated RA

explanation.surface: A painter selects a complicated subject for his next canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex' is the psychoanalytic term, not 'complicated'. RA (Royal Academician) clues any famous British painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Jung named a daughter's attachment to her father after this figure, so she is the subject of that complex.

clue.text: Game decided by what's in Chambers?

definitions.text: Game decided by what's in Chambers?

parts.words: Game decided by what's in Chambers?
parts.note: seems to be a word game settled by the Chambers dictionary, but the chambers are those of a revolver, one holding a bullet

explanation.surface: A word game whose disputes are settled by looking things up in the Chambers dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers is the dictionary crossword setters use; here it is the cylinder of a revolver.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadly gamble in which a player spins a revolver loaded with a single round and fires at their own head.

clue.text: Mother of Minos, in Crete, ready to meet father

parts.note: ready means cash, and the cash used in Crete, part of Greece, is the euro
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: In Crete, the mother of the legendary king is prepared to meet her father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is slang for money, as in 'the readies'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Zeus carried off the Phoenician princess Europa to Crete, where she bore him Minos.

clue.text: Zola's foremost cutting novel is mad at clandestine publishing

indicators.note: cutting means the letter slices into the anagram, landing inside it
novel as an adjective means new, so the letters of is mad at take a new form
foremost picks just the opening letter of Zola's

explanation.surface: A critic is furious that a leading French novelist's book has been cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges ISMADAT to SAMIDAT, and 'cutting' puts Z (from 'foremost' of Zola's) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian term for the secret copying and circulation of banned writing in the Soviet Union.

clue.text: Poems bursting with heart and feeling

indicators.note: bursting means the letters of the two words explode and are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Verses overflowing with emotion and deep sentiment.
explanation.walkthrough: The ten letters of POEMS and HEART together are shuffled; 'with' joins the two.
explanation.definitionFit: The mood or tone of a place or a work is its prevailing feeling.

clue.text: Theatre newspaper head office features in Behan's play

indicators.note: features means contains, so the newspaper's name has the next piece within it

parts.note: The Stage is the British weekly newspaper of the theatre industry

explanation.surface: A theatre paper's headquarters appears in a review of a play by Brendan Behan.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stage is a London trade paper for actors and theatre people; HO goes between its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Brendan Behan's 1958 play about an English soldier held captive by the IRA in Dublin.

clue.text: Victim of a vampire that is threatening, but no Tory

indicators.note: but no tells us to take a word away from the longer synonym

parts.note: minatory is a formal word for threatening
a Tory is a British Conservative, taken here as written

explanation.surface: A menacing figure preys on a victim, but no Conservative politician is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' simply links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Mina Harker is the young woman Count Dracula bites in Bram Stoker's novel.

clue.text: Youngster playing around like a Middlemarch cleric

indicators.note: around means the youngster's word goes round the next piece

parts.note: a cub is a youngster, a young animal or a junior scout
as a means like a
on means playing, as an actor on stage

explanation.surface: A child messing about, behaving like a clergyman from a George Eliot novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like' is not a link word: 'like a' gives AS A, which sits inside CUB.
explanation.definitionFit: The Reverend Edward Casaubon is the dry scholar-clergyman Dorothea marries in Middlemarch.

clue.text: Censor of old going on about Troy

annotationWithheld.why: Censor of old going on about Troy (4): CATO, but no sound parse found for 'going on about Troy' giving CATO (CA for about leaves TO unexplained by 'going on' and 'Troy')
annotationWithheld.clue: Censor of old going on about Troy

clue.text: Musical boxes etched on top by a plotter

indicators.note: boxes means the musical's name encloses the next piece

parts.note: Cats is the Andrew Lloyd Webber musical

indicators.note: on top picks out the leading letter of etched

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Musical boxes engraved on the lid are made by a schemer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical boxes' reads as one object, but Musical is CATS and 'boxes' is the container signal around E.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Catesby led the 1605 Gunpowder Plot to blow up Parliament.

clue.text: Delight a fruit gives a naturalist

parts.note: joy means delight
taken as written
a damson is a small purple plum

explanation.surface: The pleasure that a piece of fruit gives to a nature lover.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Born Free, who raised Elsa the lioness in Kenya, was a naturalist.

clue.text: Part of this is emended after upsetting a goddess

indicators.note: after upsetting means the letters are taken once turned over, so they read upwards
part of means the letters lie within the run this is emended

explanation.surface: Part of this text has been corrected after it caused offence to a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' takes SISEMEN from 'this is emended', and 'after upsetting' reads it from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis is the Greek goddess of retribution, who punishes arrogance.

clue.text: A novelist's key function is probing

indicators.note: is probing means the next piece pokes into the key's name

parts.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard
cot is short for cotangent, a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A writer's main purpose is investigation.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'novelist's' stands for 'is', joining definition and wordplay; COT goes inside ALT.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisa May Alcott, author of Little Women, was an American novelist.

clue.text: Nasty poster almost bound to show a novelist

indicators.note: almost tells us to drop the final letter of the word

parts.note: an internet troll posts nasty messages online
to lope is to run with long bounding strides

explanation.surface: A vile online commenter, nearly obliged to reveal himself as a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' looks like 'obliged' but is the verb to leap, LOPE; 'to show' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope wrote the Barsetshire novels, so he was a Victorian novelist.

clue.text: Emollient bandages applied primarily by a donkey-beater

indicators.note: bandages means the soothing word wraps round the next pieces

parts.note: balm is a soothing emollient ointment

indicators.note: primarily picks the opening letter of applied

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A soothing ointment is wrapped round wounds by a man who beats his donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bandages' is a verb, the container signal. In Numbers 22 the prophet Balaam beats his donkey, which then speaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Balaam is the Old Testament prophet who struck his ass three times until an angel intervened.

clue.text: A degree to teach after retiring

parts.note: taken as written
the BEd, Bachelor of Education, is the degree that qualifies a teacher

explanation.surface: Getting a teaching degree after leaving one's job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' looks like stopping work but means going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Once you have gone to bed for the night you are in bed.

clue.text: Editor with Times to call in order to reveal Betjeman's work

parts.note: to summon is to call someone in
by can mean with, as in by hand
bells mark the times, as ship's bells do the watches

explanation.surface: An editor at The Times orders a call to reveal a poet's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' says the pieces are rearranged from clue order into answer order; 'to reveal' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: John Betjeman's 1960 verse autobiography is one of his best-known works.

clue.text: Flower's positive force leads to this zen-like ease

parts.note: in Chinese thought yang is the positive, active force paired with yin

indicators.note: leads means the opening letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A flower's positive energy leads to a Zen-like calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a thing that flows, a river; the 's is 'is', a link. 'leads' picks T, Z, E from 'this zen-like ease'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yangtze is China's longest river, and in crosswords a river is something that flows.

clue.text: Grammarian Aelius, fellows must absorb at university

indicators.note: must absorb means the fellows' word takes the next pieces inside it

parts.note: dons are fellows of a university college
taken as written

explanation.surface: College fellows have to take in an ancient grammarian while at university.
explanation.definitionFit: Aelius Donatus was a fourth-century Roman teacher of grammar, whose textbook was used for centuries.
